findings.evidence: “`Bash`, `AskUserQuestion` (with `multiSelect`) and `Read` name the host's shell, structured-question and file-reading tools.” This restates familiar tool capabilities; the useful instruction is how to preserve owner consent and multi-select when the question tool is unavailable.
findings.fix: Keep the numbered plain-text fallback, multi-select behavior and requirement to wait for the owner. Drop only the generic tool glossary and record that removal.

findings.evidence: The 1,019-character description opens with “detects installed CLIs and models, proposes a review set and an execute set” and leads with wizard mechanics rather than the user's goal. The triggers and exclusions are otherwise specific.
findings.fix: Use to set up, refresh, or check ai-kit's cross-AI review and execute lanes: choose which CLIs and models review plans or implement them, and set each role's fallback order in the `[lanes]` table of `.aikit/config.toml`. Use even if the user never says “lanes,” when review or execute reports no configured lanes, when an opencode lane's provider disappears, or for migration guidance on an old `review-spec.toml`. The project file is the default; `--local` and `--global` select the layer without granting replacement consent. `--check-only` reports availability without writing config. Not for running configured lanes, hand-editing one lane, or editing `[runner]` or `opencode.jsonc`.

findings.evidence: “Step 1.6 — Sort unknown skills (optional)” keeps the full advisory, confirmation and persistence procedure in the 442-line, roughly 6,700-word body, even for runs with nothing to sort. The existing reference gates are otherwise strong.
findings.fix: Keep the listing command, the `unsorted` trigger and the independent-write warning in the main flow. Move the advisory interpretation and per-role confirmation procedure into `references/skill-role-sort.md`, loaded only when the listing has unsorted entries and the owner chooses to sort them.

findings.evidence: “Run: `models-config --sources <source-list>`” writes to the command's current project by default. This optional write appears before the lane target is normally resolved and supplies neither the confirmed project root nor a separate layer choice.
findings.fix: Treat a `[models]` change as a separate write. Default to `models-config --cwd <project root> --sources <source-list>` after naming the destination; use `--global` only when the owner explicitly chooses the user layer. Keep catalog-field corrections on `confirm-model`.

findings.evidence: The prompt says “test it,” but its expected output and assertion depend on a declined test, with `files: []` and no scripted decline. The stale catalog case at line 90 likewise has no prior catalog or current listing fixture to establish staleness.
findings.fix: Supply a scripted owner decline and a fixture for the unconfirmed profile, then assert both that no test call ran and that the saved lane was reported as untested. Give the stale-model eval a prior catalog row and a successful current listing that omits it.

findings.evidence: The suite has 11 positives and 10 negatives. Several negatives, such as “Create a new SKILL.md for a changelog generator from scratch,” do less to test the boundary than an adjacent config request would.
findings.fix: Keep the existing lane-versus-execution near-misses. Replace the unrelated changelog and GSD phase prompts with requests to inspect an existing trust decision and to edit `[models]` settings without changing the roster. Consolidate the two stale-provider positives to reach a 10/10 split.

findings.evidence: “Just check my reviewers, change nothing” enters `--check-only`, but a confirmed read-only profile bypasses its risk question and the probe can still write runner state, clear leftovers, or spend quota. Project read-only status does not make the probe side-effect-free.
findings.fix: Route an explicit no-change request to detection, read-only roster inspection and `check-providers`, reporting quota availability as unknown. Offer the live probe separately after disclosing runner-state and quota effects, even when all invocation profiles are read-only.

findings.evidence: “A custom command's placeholder filled from another lane field can change the launched argv without changing the list.” The next instruction still allows the live probe on an unchanged list, so the owner's consent can cover a different invocation from the one run.
findings.fix: For custom entries, make consent cover the resolved argument list and probe that same validated snapshot. If the runner cannot bind the probe to the reviewed invocation, report the affected availability as unknown and skip the probe.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list calls `REVIEW/EXECUTE` the literal `purpose` values, but Steps 2.6–2.7 and the writer contract require `review`, `execute`, or `both`. Following the uppercase instruction can cause a lane to be rejected.
findings.fix: State the stored literals as `review`, `execute`, and `both`. If `REVIEW` and `EXECUTE` are used as display headings, distinguish them from serialized values.

findings.evidence: The unmatched-candidate branch supplies only `{"model_id": ..., "entry": {...}}`, and the no-fetch branch points back to that form. The catalog validator requires `provider`, a nonempty `runtimes` map, `source`, `confidence`, and `last_verified`, so a first-time setup cannot construct a valid entry from the instructions alone.
findings.fix: Add one validator-accepted, annotated `--entry-json` example here, with a canonical catalog key, a runtime-to-model mapping, provenance and a date. Point the no-fetch branch to that example and say how to continue when the owner cannot supply a required field.

findings.evidence: “codex has no `models`/`list-models` subcommand (confirmed via `codex --help`)” is an undated claim about the vendor CLI's command surface. The wizard reads ai-kit's enumeration live but does not instruct the agent to verify that separate absence claim.
findings.fix: Base the wizard's decision on whether `detect-runtimes` actually returned a `models` list. Keep the Codex command-surface detail as a dated observation linked to official source, or verify it with the installed binary's help when diagnosing a listing failure.
